title: The fixture repository is created with subprocess.run(['git','init',...], env={**os.environ, 'GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL': devnull, 'GIT_CONFIG_NOSYS
description: The fixture repository is created with subprocess.run(['git','init',...], env={**os.environ, 'GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL': devnull, 'GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM': '1'}). The ambient GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_INDEX_FILE, GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY, GIT_COMMON_DIR and similar variables are inherited. Git hooks such as pre-commit export GIT_INDEX_FILE and sometimes GIT_DIR. When pytest is launched from such a context, 'git init' initialises or reinitialises the host repository instead of tmp_path/repo, and the later toplevel discovery from src/pkg resolves against the host. The test's CONFIG_INVALID and .env expectations then fail. Whether it fails depends on how the suite was launched, not on a random draw. The Rust side already strips these variables (crates/sc-agent-types/src/git.rs lines 98-102, and the git() helpers in crates/sc-jev-check/tests/repo.rs and crates/sc-jev-host/tests/log_context.rs), so this is the one fixture that does not.
